## Proof

Let $A$ be the ground ring (or field) and let $G(k,n)$ denote the Grassmannian of rank-$k$ direct summands of $A^{\oplus n}$. Write an ordered basis $v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ as the invertible matrix $V\in\mathrm{GL}_n(A)$ whose $i$-th column is $v_i$; similarly $w$ gives $W$. The **change-of-basis matrix** is

$$g \;=\; V^{-1}W \;\in\; \mathrm{GL}_n(A), \qquad\text{so that}\qquad w_j=\sum_{i} g_{ij}\,v_i \;\;(W=Vg).$$

A vector $x\in A^{\oplus n}$ with $v$-coordinates $a$ (i.e. $x=Va$) has $w$-coordinates $b=g^{-1}a$, since $x=Wb=Vgb$.

### The affine charts

For a $k$-element subset $I\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$ define the standard open set

$$U_{v,I}\;=\;\bigl\{\,M\in G(k,n)\;:\; M\to \operatorname{span}(v_i,\,i\in I)\text{ is an isomorphism}\,\bigr\}.$$

Identifying $A^{\oplus n}\cong A^n$ via $v$, a point $M\in U_{v,I}$ is the column-span of an $n\times k$ matrix whose $I$-rows form an invertible $k\times k$ block. Multiplying on the left by the inverse of that block normalises the $I$-rows to $I_k$, leaving the complementary rows as a free parameter $X\in A^{(n-k)\times k}\cong \mathbb{A}^{k(n-k)}$. Thus

$$\varphi_{v,I}:\; U_{v,I}\;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;\mathbb{A}^{k(n-k)},\qquad M\;\mapsto\; X,$$

where $M=\operatorname{colspan}\bigl(N_v(X)\bigr)$ and $N_v(X)$ is the $n\times k$ matrix with $I$-rows $=I_k$ and $I^c$-rows $=X$. The chart $U_w$ is defined analogously, using a $k$-subset $J$ and the basis $w$.

### Where the gluing is valid

The two charts are simultaneously defined on the overlap

$$U_{v,I}\;\cap\; U_{w,J}\;=\;\bigl\{\,M\;:\; M\to\operatorname{span}(v_I)\text{ and }M\to\operatorname{span}(w_J)\text{ are both isomorphisms}\,\bigr\}.$$

In the $(v,I)$-chart this is the locus where the $J$-rows of the $w$-coordinate representative of $M$ are invertible. Converting $v$-coordinates to $w$-coordinates multiplies every coordinate column by $g^{-1}$, so the $w$-coordinate matrix of $M=\operatorname{colspan}(N_v(X))$ is

$$N_w(X)\;=\;g^{-1}\,N_v(X).$$

Hence the overlap, read inside the affine space $\mathbb{A}^{k(n-k)}$ of the $(v,I)$-chart, is the **principal open set**

$$\Omega_{v,I}^{w,J}\;=\;\bigl\{\,X\in\mathbb{A}^{k(n-k)}\;:\;\det\!\bigl((g^{-1}N_v(X))_{J}\bigr)\in A^{\times}\,\bigr\},$$

i.e. the non-vanishing locus of the $k\times k$ minor obtained from the $J$-rows of $g^{-1}N_v(X)$. The gluing is valid precisely on this open set (and its image in the $(w,J)$-chart), because there — and only there — both normalisations are legitimate: the $I$-block of $N_v(X)$ is $I_k$ by construction, and the $J$-block of $N_w(X)$ is invertible by the defining condition of $\Omega$.

### The transition map and the role of $g$

On $\Omega_{v,I}^{w,J}$ the $(w,J)$-coordinate $Y$ is obtained by normalising the $J$-rows of $N_w(X)=g^{-1}N_v(X)$ to $I_k$:

$$\boxed{\;Y \;=\; \bigl(g^{-1}N_v(X)\bigr)_{J^{c}}\;\cdot\;\bigl(g^{-1}N_v(X)\bigr)_{J}^{\,-1}\;}$$

where the subscripts mean "rows indexed by $J$" / "rows indexed by $J^{c}$". This is a morphism of affine varieties (a regular map on the principal open set, since the inverse exists there), with inverse obtained by exchanging the roles of $v,w$ and replacing $g$ by $g^{-1}$:

$$X \;=\; \bigl(g\,N_w(Y)\bigr)_{I^{c}}\;\cdot\;\bigl(g\,N_w(Y)\bigr)_{I}^{\,-1}.$$

The **change-of-basis matrix $g=V^{-1}W$** enters in exactly two places, both forced by the coordinate change $a\mapsto g^{-1}a$:

1. **Domain of the transition** — the open set $\Omega$ is cut out by invertibility of a $k\times k$ minor of $g^{-1}N_v(X)$; this minor is a polynomial in the entries of $X$ with coefficients drawn from $g^{-1}$, so the shape of the overlap is governed by $g$.
2. **Formula for the transition** — the regular map $X\mapsto Y$ is built out of $g^{-1}N_v(X)$ and its inverse block, so the analytic expression of the gluing isomorphism is determined by $g$.

### Cocycle condition

If a third basis $u$ with change-of-basis $h=W^{-1}U$ (so $u=w\,h$, and $v\to u$ uses $gh$) is introduced, then on a triple overlap $U_{v,I}\cap U_{w,J}\cap U_{u,K}$ the composed transition $X\mapsto Y\mapsto Z$ equals the direct transition $X\mapsto Z$ computed from $(gh)^{-1}=h^{-1}g^{-1}$, because coordinate conversion is simply right-multiplication by the cumulative change-of-basis matrix and matrix multiplication is associative. Thus the transition functions satisfy the cocycle condition

$$\varphi_{u,K;\,w,J}\circ\varphi_{w,J;\,v,I}\;=\;\varphi_{u,K;\,v,I},$$

and the three patches glue consistently. By varying $I,J,K$ over all $k$-subsets and $v,w,u$ over all bases, the affine patches $\{U_{v,I}\}$ assemble into the Grassmannian $G(k,n)$ as a scheme, with all gluings mediated by the corresponding change-of-basis matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(A)$.

---

**Summary.** Two affine patches $U_v=U_{v,I}$ and $U_w=U_{w,J}$ are glued along the open subset of $\mathbb{A}^{k(n-k)}$ on which the $J$-row minor of $g^{-1}N_v(X)$ is invertible, where $g=V^{-1}W$ is the change-of-basis matrix converting $v$-coordinates into $w$-coordinates. On this open set the transition is the regular map $Y=(g^{-1}N_v(X))_{J^c}\,(g^{-1}N_v(X))_J^{-1}$; its inverse is obtained by replacing $g$ with $g^{-1}$, and the cocycle condition follows from associativity of matrix multiplication. Hence the gluing is valid exactly where both charts are simultaneously defined, and the change-of-basis matrix $g$ completely determines both the domain and the formula of the gluing isomorphism.
